title: Automate a repetitive process from a recorded walkthrough
description: A system that turns one recorded walkthrough into a numbered SOP someone else could follow.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

batch-api.title: Batch API
batch-api.content: A way to send a big pile of requests to Claude at once and get the results back later (usually within 24 hours) at a discount. Good for one-time bulk jobs like classifying 10,000 customer support tickets.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

personal-knowledge-base.title: Personal Knowledge Base
personal-knowledge-base.content: A store of your own accumulated knowledge — notes, decisions, references — organized so an AI can search and use it. The difference from a pile of documents: structure and maintenance. Level 2 builds one as a wiki.

children.text: [Atlassian's State of Teams 2024 research](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/state-of-teams-2024) found 55% of knowledge workers say it's hard to track down information at work despite knowing plenty of people who could help, a clear sign of a process still living in one person's head instead of a doc. This system takes a recorded walkthrough, a screen share with narration, or someone just talking through the steps, and turns the transcript into a numbered SOP with verification steps and a troubleshooting section.

The same research found teams that consolidate work and knowledge on a shared platform spend 50% less time searching for information, the payoff once a walkthrough becomes a real doc. Steps land in the order performed rather than a cleaned-up ideal, workarounds get called out separately from the standard path, and any step the person skipped without explaining gets flagged. Whoever recorded the walkthrough reviews the draft against what they meant before it counts as the process.

Run it as a one-time paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) for a single process, a saved skill for whoever documents processes regularly, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that watches a folder of new recordings and drafts the SOP on its own. Every version stops at a draft a person approves.
Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming the process, how you'll capture it, who the SOP is for, and where the finished doc lives.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns me talking through a process out loud, or a screen recording, into a real SOP someone else could follow without me in the room. Ask me questions, one at a time, about which process to start with, how I'll capture it, who the SOP is for, what "done right" looks like, and where the finished doc should live. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview forces decisions about capture method and audience up front, before you're staring at a raw transcript guessing what the SOP is for.

items: Which tool captures the walkthrough, and whether it auto-generates a transcript.
Where the finished SOP lives so people find it.
Who reviews and approves it before it's treated as the real process.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by asking a different [model](#tooltip-model) to poke holes, then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your recording or transcription tool (Zoom, Loom, Otter.ai), your documentation home ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Confluence, Google Docs, a shared drive), and your team chat tool to announce the new SOP. The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build the system your scope document describes and test it on a real walkthrough transcript. The prompt below is an example; your scope document gives you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn a transcript of me walking through [process name] into a numbered SOP that [new hire/teammate] could follow without asking me anything.

Context: Transcript at [file location]. This process uses [tool names from the walkthrough]. The person following it will have [access level, prior knowledge].

Rules:
- Number steps in the order actually performed, not a cleaned-up ideal order.
- Call out workarounds or exceptions separately from the standard path.
- Flag any step where I skipped an explanation.
- Output: numbered steps, a "before you start" checklist, and a troubleshooting table.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: ordering steps by what happened keeps the SOP matching reality instead of turning into an idealized description no one follows exactly.

children.text: **Review.** Check the draft against your scope. Real order, workarounds separated out, troubleshooting covering the likely failures?
**Feedback.** Tell it what's wrong and fold the fix into the rules.

items: [Batch](#tooltip-batch-api) it across every process leaving with a departing employee.
Flag where two SOPs describe the same task differently.
Turn a growing SOP library into onboarding material.
Feed it into an internal [knowledge base](#tooltip-personal-knowledge-base) bot as the library grows.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat draft the rubric and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each SOP, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for process name, date documented, steps confirmed accurate, corrections needed, and reviewer. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns show which processes need a re-record once the steps change.

children.text: **Log** every SOP you generate against the rubric. Note the date and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from the log. Once the rubric passes a few runs straight, package the prompt and rules into a reusable AI skill. A repeated miss is your next candidate. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill interviews you and writes it; a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).

One durable failure mode. A transcript captures what someone did, so a bad habit narrated clearly still turns into a clean, wrong SOP. Check the draft against what the process should be before anyone follows it.
